[[File:Glen Sather, 2006 NHL Awards (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Glen Sather]] coached the Rangers for 90 games between 2003 and 2004.]]
The [[New York Rangers]] are a professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[New York City]]. They are members of the [[Metropolitan Division]] of the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). Playing their home games at [[Madison Square Garden]], the Rangers are one of the oldest teams in the NHL, having joined in 1926 as an expansion franchise, and are part of the group of teams referred to as the [[Original Six]]. The Rangers were the first NHL franchise in the United States to win the [[Stanley Cup]],<ref name="Rangers Bruins">{{cite web |last1=Anderson |first1=Dave |title=Sports of The Times; At Boston Garden, There's Much More Gold Than Green |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/05/14/sports/sports-of-the-times-at-boston-garden-there-s-much-more-gold-than-green.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=May 12, 2021 |date=May 14, 1995 |archive-date=January 31, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130131065831/http://www.nytimes.com/1995/05/14/sports/sports-of-the-times-at-boston-garden-there-s-much-more-gold-than-green.html |url-status=live }}</ref> which they have done four times (most recently in [[1994 Stanley Cup Final|1994]]).<ref name="Rangers Cup">{{cite web |last1=Vecsey |first1=George |title=Sports of The Times; Houston Finally Has an Edge |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/06/23/sports/sports-of-the-times-houston-finally-has-an-edge.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=May 12, 2021 |date=June 23, 1994 |archive-date=May 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210512161554/https://www.nytimes.com/1994/06/23/sports/sports-of-the-times-houston-finally-has-an-edge.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The team is commonly referred to by its famous nickname, "The Broadway Blueshirts", or more commonly in New York media, as simply the "Blueshirts".

There have been thirty-seven head coaches for the Rangers, the first one being [[Lester Patrick]], and the most recent being [[Peter Laviolette]]. [[Muzz Patrick]], [[Alfred Pike]], and [[Ron Smith (ice hockey, born 1944)|Ron Smith]] are the only coaches who spent their entire careers with the Rangers and were not elected to the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]].<ref name="Muzz Patrick"/><ref name="Pike"/><ref name="Smith"/><ref name="Campbell"/> [[Bernie Geoffrion]], [[Lynn Patrick]], [[Emile Francis]], [[Glen Sather]], [[Craig Patrick]], [[Roger Neilson]], [[Herb Brooks]], and [[Fred Shero]] have all been inducted to the Hockey Hall of Fame.<ref name="Geoffrion"/><ref name="Lynn"/><ref name="Francis"/><ref name="Sather"/><ref name="Craig Patrick"/><ref name="Neilson"/><ref name="Brooks"/><ref name="Shero"/> [[Lester Patrick]], [[Frank Boucher]], [[Colin Campbell (ice hockey executive)|Colin Campbell]], [[Neil Colville]], [[Bill Cook]], [[Phil Esposito]], [[Doug Harvey (ice hockey)|Doug Harvey]], and [[Bryan Trottier]] have all coached the Rangers for their entire coaching careers and have been elected to the Hockey Hall of Fame.<ref name="Patrick"/><ref name="Boucher"/><ref name="Colville"/><ref name="Cook"/><ref name="Esposito"/><ref name="Harvey"/><ref name="Trottier"/> [[Emile Francis]] has coached the most regular season games, 654, and the most playoff games, 75, in franchise history. [[Emile Francis]] also holds the franchise records in regular season wins, 342, and playoff wins, 34. [[Mike Keenan]], the twenty-fifth head coach of the Rangers, amassed the best points percentage, .667, and regular season winning percentage, .619, having done so in a single, 84-game season. Keenan is also the only head coach to have coached the Rangers to a [[Presidents' Trophy]] and [[Stanley Cup]] in the same season.<ref name="Keenan"/> [[Lester Patrick]] is the only head coach to have coached the Rangers to multiple Stanley Cups. Under head coach Peter Laviolette the Rangers set franchise records in wins (55) and points (114) in a single season, having set both records in the [[2023–24 NHL season|2023–24 season]].<ref name="Laviolette"/> The [[Jack Adams Award]] has never been awarded to the head coach of the [[New York Rangers]].
